PAYMENT OF WAGES (PROCEDURE) RULES,
1937
[Published in the Gazette of India, under
Department of Industries and Labour Noti fication No. L‑3067, dated 24
February, 1937.]
[Rules made by Central Government under Sub‑section (1) of
section 26 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (1 V of 1936) read with section 22
of the General Clause Act, 1897 (X of 1897) after previous publication as
required by sub‑section (3) of section 26 of the Act).]
1. Short title.‑-- These rules nary be called the Payment of
Wages (Pro cedure) Rules, 1937.
2. Definitions.---‑ In these rates, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject of context;‑‑‑‑
(a) "the Act" means the Payment of
Wages Act, 1936 (IV of 1935);
(b) "appeal" means an appeal under
section 17 ;
(c) "the Authority" means the
authority appointed under sub‑section (1) of section 15;
(d) "the Court" means the Court
mentioned in sub‑section (1) of sec tion 17;
(e) "employer"
included the persons responsible spat fat payment of wages under section 3;
(f) "section" means a section of the
Act;
(g) "form" means a form appended to
these rules;
(h) word and expressions defined ire the Act
shall be deemed to have the same meaning as in the Act.
3. Form of Application‑--- Applications under sub‑section
(2) of section 15 by or on behalf of an employed person or group of employed
parsons shall be made in duplicate in Form A, Form B or Form as the case clay
be, one copy of which shall bear such court‑fee as may be prescribed.
4. Authorisation.‑‑‑ The authorization to act on
behalf of an employed person or persons, under section 15 shall be given by a
certificate in Form D shall be presented to the Authority hearing the
application anal shall form part of the record.
5. Permission to appear: --- Any person desiring the permission of
the Authority to act on behalf of any employed person or persons shall present
to the Authority a brief written statement explaining his interest in the
matter and the Authority shall record an order on the statement, which in the
case of refusal shall include reasons for the order, said shall incorporate it
in the record.
6. Presentation of documents.‑--- (1) Applications or other
documents relevant to an application may be presented in person to the
Authority at any time during hours to be fixed by the Authority, or may be sent
to him by registered post.
(2) The
Authority shall at once endorse, or cause to be endorsed, on each document the
date of the presentation or receipt, as the case may be.
7. Refusal to entertain application.‑-- (1) The Authority may
refuse to entertain an application presented under rule 6, if after giving the
applicant an opportunity of being heard, the Authority is satisfied, for
reasons to be recorded in writing that
(a) the application is not entitled to present
an application, or
(b) the application if
barred by reason of the provisions in the pro visos to sub‑section (2) of
section 15, or
(c) the applicant shows no sufficient cause for
making a direction under section 15.
(2) The
Authority may refuse to entertain an application which is insufficiently
stamped or is otherwise incomplete and; if he so refuses, shall return it at
once with an indication of the defects. If the application is presented again
after the defects have been made good, the date of represen tation shall be
deemed to be the date of presentation for the purposes of the provisos to sub‑section
(9) of section 15.
8. Appearance of parties.‑--- (1) If the application is
entertained the Authority shall call upon the employer by a notice in Form E to
appear before him on a specified dated together with all relevant documents and
witnesses, if any, and shall inform the applicant of the date so specified.

employer or his representative fails to appear on the specified date, the
